questions.stem: A team moving a Java 8 service onto Java 21 relied on a Security Manager policy. What does the page point them to instead?

options.text: A stricter policy file, loaded through the java.security.manager property
options.says: The Security Manager is deprecated for removal; a stricter policy for it is not the page's way forward.

options.text: The module system plus narrower mechanisms, each built for one purpose
options.says: With the Security Manager deprecated, the page recommends the module system and other targeted mechanisms instead.

options.text: A sandbox that runs the service's own code as untrusted applet code
options.says: Applets and their sandbox are gone; the page points to the module system and targeted mechanisms.

questions.stem: An order's quantity is already checked by the API layer. According to the page, what should the service and persistence layers do about that quantity?

options.text: Accept it as given, because the API layer has already checked it
options.says: The page warns against relying on a single layer of validation.

options.text: Only encode it for storage, because checking it again adds no safety
options.says: Encoding is not the rule the page gives here; it asks for validation at every boundary as defense in depth.

options.text: Check it again at their own boundary, as one more line of defense
options.says: Defense in depth: the page says to validate at every boundary, the API, service and persistence layers.
